Both ligands are generation-1 probes of mine. Ligand 1 is the picolinamide-cap version at jnk3 0.43 - the second azine on the cap cost 0.07 of activity and 0.12 of QED, so that idea is closed. Atom 0 is its pyridine 4-methyl over an acyclic bond, the anchor, which means whatever I build keeps a methyl somewhere; the sensible place is the azine C4 where it belongs. That constrains this episode to a 4-methyl molecule, so I will use it to settle a comparison I left confounded. My best molecule has a 4-chloro and a cyclobutyl cap and scores 0.52; the best 4-methyl molecule has a cyclopropyl cap and scores 0.50. Two variables differ, so I cannot say whether chlorine is actually worth anything. Building the 4-methyl with a cyclobutyl cap puts the two on the same cap and isolates the halogen. It is also worth having on its own merits: the 4-methyl azines consistently post QED around 0.903 against 0.889 for the chloro, so if chlorine turns out to be worth nothing, the methyl version is the better molecule.
